lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The dark did not leave us a world. It left us choices.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the sword. The dead on unfinished roads still carry coin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stand on a road seal and press B. Spend what you earn, and decide what exists next.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A hero. How novel. I was napping.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That branch beside me? Take it. Hold it into my fire and it wakes as a TORCH.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Two hearths in this clearing sit cold. Carry the flame to them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Burnt brush leaves CHARCOAL. Put it in the marked box: the balloon calls the plane, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My ship broke into samples all over this crater.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the PICKAXE. It cracks rock — and rock is where the good things hide.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Plain stone breaks. The VEINED boulders never do: three good swings, one lump of IRON, forever.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The lab buys every lump you carry. Mining is honest pay out here.

trade.offer: Iron! The lab pays 3 coins a lump. How many are you selling?
trade.empty: Your pack has no iron. The veined boulders — three good swings each, they never run dry.
trade.thanks: Prime samples. Pleasure doing science with you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Timber. That is the market now.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: This AXE is yours — consider it an advance. It fells DEAD wood in a chop or two.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My dry ranks stand in rows. Clear them, and the sticks are pure profit.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Sticks build bridges. Bridges open markets. Work hard.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Suit says the pool up north-east glows. Molten ground is no road.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take this STONE. Throw it into lava and it cools into a basalt step.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Something metal sank by the little island. One good step opens the route.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The basalt stays behind. Cross back carrying whatever you find.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Zero! Perfect timing. This field is a canvas, and it is BLANK.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take these SEEDS. My pigments. The beds along the south edge are already dug.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stand before a bed and press A to plant. Water wakes them — rain, or a bucket.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Green is a colour you GROW. Paint me a meadow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Friend! You look thirsty. Or dry. Either way — opportunity.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Free sample: this BUCKET. Fill it in my pond, just west of the fire.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A full bucket waters crops and drowns small fires. Endless uses. Zero coins. Today only.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Tell your friends. If you find any out there.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The pines sing, but they crowd the verse.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: This GREAT AXE fells even LIVING trees — the small axe only knows dead wood.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Open a clearing in my grove. Listen how the song changes where light falls.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Every good line needs its silence. Cut me one.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Do not be alarmed. I am off duty.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the SCYTHE. It reaps the tall grass in one clean sweep — press A before it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Cut grass surrenders SEEDS. Life insists on returning. It always does.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The meadow here grew loud. Quiet it for me, and we are even.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Dead wood. Your sword will not move it — a blade cuts what bleeds.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The AXE is at my feet. Take it, face a dead tree, and press X. Four swings and it comes down.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A felled tree leaves a STICK behind. Put those sticks in the marked box: the balloon calls the plane, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Behind that wall there is iron, and nothing guarding it. Nothing walks in here. Take your time. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. My hearth is lit. Yours is a stick on the ground.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the STICK. Face my fire and press X: it wakes as a TORCH. It burns for a while and then it dies — come back and light it again.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Dry brush cannot be chopped. It BURNS. Touch one with the torch and the fire walks to its neighbours on its own.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Burnt brush leaves CHARCOAL on the ground. Put it in the marked box: the balloon calls the plane, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Stone does not burn and it does not chop. It BREAKS.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The PICKAXE is at my feet. Face a rock, press X, and press it again. The rock opens and leaves a STONE where it stood.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The boulders with red veins never open. Every three blows they spit out ORE instead — and they never run dry.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ore is not iron. That is a lesson for a hotter day. Put the ORE in the marked box and the plane pays in coin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Take the SWORD. Press Z — and press it again, and again.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Nothing here falls to one blow. Strike a body that is still flashing and your blade slides off it: that flash is a body that cannot be hurt yet. Wait a beat.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And watch their feet. When one plants itself and winds up, it is GUARDING the side it faces. Hitting that side gives you sparks and nothing else — walk around it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hold Z instead of tapping it and the blade spins: it cuts all eight neighbours at once. Mrrow. Go on.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The marked box takes the IRON you earned here. Load it, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Water. You cannot swim and you cannot chop it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: One tile of that bank will take a crossing. Face it and press X holding TWO STICKS and you nail a plank deck. Or hold ONE STONE and you drop a ford.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: They carry you the same. They do not carry FIRE the same: flame runs across planks and eats them. It stops dead at stone, every time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: So the question is never "how do I cross". It is: do I want a floor here, or a fuse? Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The marked box takes the IRON you earned here. Load it, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. That rock is not going anywhere. No pick in the world opens it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: But look at the ground — one tile is MARKED. That is where the stone is thin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take a BOMB and stand on the mark: it arms itself the moment you get there, and it counts. Then leave. Three of them on the floor, so you may waste two learning.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Everything you carry that burns, burns on its own clock. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The marked box takes the IRON you earned here. Load it, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Two gates, same wood, same hinge. Walk into the top one.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It shudders and stays shut. Nothing is locked — there is a BOULDER sitting against its back, and a gate that swings inward cannot swing through stone.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The lower one has nothing behind it. Walk into that one and it gives.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: No key exists for either. A swing gate only ever asks one thing: is the tile behind me empty? Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The marked box takes the IRON you earned here. Load it, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. The way through is a FLOWER, and it is shut.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It is shut because of my fire. That bud opens in the dark and closes in the light — it has no opinion about you at all.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the BUCKET. Face the puddle and press X to fill it; face the fire and press X to throw it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Water is the only thing in this world that puts fire OUT. Everything else you own only starts them. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The marked box takes the IRON you earned here. Load it, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. That door wants ONE BAR OF IRON. You have no iron. You have rust-stained rock.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Face the FURNACE and press Z: it knows two recipes, and one of them turns ore and charcoal into a bloom. Confirming does not hand it to you — it LIGHTS the furnace. Wait for it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: What jumps out is a sponge, not a bar. Carry it to the stone ALTAR, press Z to lay it down, then beat it. Three blows and the slag is gone.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Then take the bar with B. Ore, fire, hammer, bar — there is no shortcut, and every forge in this world runs that order. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The marked box takes the IRON you earned here. Load it, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Take the SCYTHE and cut that tall grass. What it leaves behind is SEEDS.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Now the SHOVEL. Face bare earth — plain dirt, not stone — and press X. It opens a hole.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Walk over the hole while you carry seeds and they sow themselves. Then fill the BUCKET at the puddle with X, face the mound, and throw it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Wait a moment and it comes up as real grass: it blocks, it burns, and the scythe takes it again. The hole reopens under it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It never MULTIPLIES — one seed, one clump, forever. What a farm gives you is grass WHERE YOU WANT IT: a fuse you can lay by hand.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And the box beside me buys the spare. The sign on it shows what it takes; face it with X and it pays, coins on the ground. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The marked box takes the SEEDS you earned here. Load it, and the plane drops your coins.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Six lumps of ore. That is a hull patch and a landing strut, and I am not being poetic.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ore, fire, hammer, bar. Your ancients ran that same order — I keep digging their slag out of this crater.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: She will not fly on six. But she stopped being scrap the moment you set them down. Bring bars if you find them; the counter stays open.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And the crating from the ship went to that tower of yours. It was never going to fly. Let it burn where people can see it.

trade.offer: Iron! The lab pays 3 coins a lump. How many are you selling?
trade.empty: Your pack has no iron. The veined boulders — three good swings each, they never run dry.
trade.thanks: Prime samples. Pleasure doing science with you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Three hearths breathing where there were three cold stones. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You did not light fires. You moved a LINE — and everything on the far side of it noticed.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The ones who kept those hearths are still out there, walking. They remember warmth. That is the whole problem.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And I sent wood to that tower of yours in the open field. A cat pays in kindling. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Six sticks. Delivered. On schedule. Do you know how rare that is out here?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And do you know what a stick is worth in a dark this size? Everything. A bridge, a fire, a night somebody survives.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: So I will keep buying timber and you will keep carrying flame. Different trades. Same fuel.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And I wrote off a bundle to that pyre of yours. Call it advertising. Everyone will see it burn.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That is the metal. It went down with the ones who came before, and you walked it back over basalt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The suit ticks twice and goes quiet.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: They worked this valley before the dark. Every bar out there was a day somebody spent. Carry it like that.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I sent my scrap timber to your pyre, too. Nothing here is worth keeping dry for long.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You GREW it. All the way down to the south beds — that is a meadow, and I did not paint it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: In a world the dark ate, green is not decoration. Green is an argument.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back when the light is low. That is the hour a field is worth the canvas.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Oh, and the cuttings went to your tower in the field. A meadow can spare a few branches for a fire that big.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stock! Actual stock! Friend, you have made me a legitimate business.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stone and sticks. One stops a fire dead, one carries it for miles. I sell both and take no side.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The bucket stays free, obviously. Water is the only thing out here that ENDS a flame — a man should give that away, not sell it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I also had a load carried to your tower. Free. Do not tell anyone — it ruins the model.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Four pines down. Listen — the grove has a rest in it now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He listens to the gap for a long time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And the light came in with the silence. That is the whole trick of this world, is it not: you cut, and the dark gets smaller.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The trunks are too good to rot here. I had them hauled to your pyre — let the grove end as a signal.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Eight of the road-dead put down, and six fields decided into being. You have been busy, Zero.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: They were the crusade before you. They kept the hearths you are relighting, and they lost. Do not hate them for still walking.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Keep spending the coin. A world that stops being decided stops being.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And the old crusade left cordwood in these ruins. It is at the pyre now, where it always meant to go.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Five hearths. And that furnace smoke again — I watched it cross three fields from right here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I was sent to CLOSE this place, hero. Instead I stand at the end of the road counting fires you lit.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go on, then. Light another. I will keep waiting — it is still the one thing I am good at.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I had wood taken to your pyre as well. Do not read anything into it. I simply prefer the road lit.
